title: COVID-19 lockdown effect on retail foot traffic

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Difference-in-Differences (DID). We compare the change in foot traffic before/after March 2020 between stores in counties with strict lockdowns (treated) versus minimal restrictions (control). Key assumption: parallel trends - stores in both groups would have followed similar foot traffic trends absent the lockdown policy intervention.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s01_data.csv")

# Basic summary statistics
cat("=== DATA SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("Total observations:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Number of stores:", length(unique(data$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Time periods:", min(data$period), "to", max(data$period), "\n")
cat("Treated stores:", sum(data$treated == 1 & data$period == 1), "\n")
cat("Control stores:", sum(data$treated == 0 & data$period == 1), "\n\n")

# Main DID regression with store and period fixed effects
did_model <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = data)

cat("=== MAIN DID RESULTS ===\n")
print(summary(did_model))

# Extract key coefficient
did_coeff <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
cat("\nKey Result: DID coefficient =", round(did_coeff, 4), "\n")
cat("Interpretation: Strict lockdowns reduced foot traffic by", 
    round(abs(did_coeff) * 100, 1), "percentage points relative to minimal restrictions\n\n")

# Pre-trend test: interact treatment with pre-period dummies
data$period_2 <- ifelse(data$period == 2, 1, 0)
data$period_3 <- ifelse(data$period == 3, 1, 0)

pretrend_model <- feols(y ~ treated:period_2 + treated:period_3 + treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                       data = data)

cat("=== PRE-TREND TEST ===\n")
print(summary(pretrend_model))

# Test joint significance of pre-trend coefficients
pretrend_pval <- waldtest(pretrend_model, "treated:period_2 = treated:period_3 = 0")$p.value
cat("Joint test p-value for pre-trends:", round(pretrend_pval, 3), "\n")
if(pretrend_pval > 0.05) {
  cat("✓ Parallel trends assumption supported (p > 0.05)\n\n")
} else {
  cat("✗ Potential violation of parallel trends (p < 0.05)\n\n")
}

# Dynamic effects: estimate treatment effects by post-period
data$period_5 <- ifelse(data$period == 5, 1, 0)
data$period_6 <- ifelse(data$period == 6, 1, 0)
data$period_7 <- ifelse(data$period == 7, 1, 0)
data$period_8 <- ifelse(data$period == 8, 1, 0)

dynamic_model <- feols(y ~ treated:period_5 + treated:period_6 + treated:period_7 + treated:period_8 | 
                      unit_id + period, data = data)

cat("=== DYNAMIC EFFECTS ===\n")
print(summary(dynamic_model))

# Calculate mean effects in post-period
post_effects <- c(coef(dynamic_model)["treated:period_5"],
                  coef(dynamic_model)["treated:period_6"], 
                  coef(dynamic_model)["treated:period_7"],
                  coef(dynamic_model)["treated:period_8"])

cat("Average post-treatment effect:", round(mean(post_effects, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")

# Robustness: Alternative specification without unit fixed effects (pooled OLS)
pooled_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS: POOLED OLS ===\n")
cat("DID coefficient (pooled):", round(coef(pooled_model)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")

# Summary of key findings
cat("\n=== SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("1. Main DID effect:", round(did_coeff, 4), "\n")
cat("2. Pre-trend test p-value:", round(pretrend_pval, 3), "\n")
cat("3. Economic significance:", round(abs(did_coeff) * 100, 1), "pp reduction in log foot traffic\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a negative coefficient around -0.3 to -0.6, indicating strict lockdowns reduced foot traffic by 30-60 percentage points relative to minimal restrictions. This aligns with the severe mobility restrictions during early COVID-19 lockdowns. The effect should be immediate and persistent across post-treatment periods, with potential intensification in the first month (March-April 2020) when lockdowns were most stringent.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=strict-lockdown counties, control=minimal-restriction counties; shock=March 2020 lockdown
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Strict-lockdown stores show significantly lower foot traffic post-lockdown
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~30% decline in foot traffic for treated stores
